## How many cells are + for grpr across treatments? 

```{r}
grpr <- subset(mydata1, subset = ENSDARG00000056620 > 0)

table(grpr$treatment)

```


```{r}

mydata_filtered <- subset(mydata1, 
                          subset = treatment %in% c("befa", "cv", "gf"))

library(ggpubr)  # Required for stat_compare_means

gene_id <- "ENSDARG00000056620"

# Create plot
plot <- VlnPlot(mydata_filtered,
                features = gene_id,
                group.by = "treatment",
                assay = "RNA",
                pt.size = 0.1,          # Smaller points for clarity
                cols = c("#1f77b4", "#ff7f0e", "#2ca02c")) +  # Custom colors
  ggtitle("GRPR Expression (BefA vs. CV vs. GF)") +
  ylab("Normalized Expression") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"))

# Add p-values
plot + stat_compare_means(
  comparisons = list(
    c("befa", "gf"),
    c("befa", "cv"),
    c("gf", "cv")  # Optional: Add GF vs. CV comparison
  ),
  method = "wilcox.test",
  label = "p.signif",
  symnum.args = list(
    cutpoints = c(0, 0.0001, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, 1),
    symbols = c("****", "***", "**", "*", "ns")),
  step.increase = 0.1  # Adjust space between brackets
)

```

```{r}
FeaturePlot(mydata1, 
            features = "ENSDARG00000056620",
            reduction = "umap",
            order = TRUE,       
            pt.size = 0.5,
            cols = c("lightgrey", "red")) +
  ggtitle("GRPR Expression Across All Cells") +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

```


## Level of expression of grpr for each cell 



```{r}

dot_plot <- DotPlot(
  mydata_filtered,
  features = "ENSDARG00000056620",
  group.by = "treatment",
  assay = "RNA",
  cols = c("lightgrey", "#E64B35"),  # Gradient from grey to red
  scale = TRUE,                      # Scale expression across groups
  dot.scale = 6                      # Adjust dot size
) +
  labs(title = "GRPR Expression Levels", y = "Treatment", x = "") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 12),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )

dot_plot
```
